title: Crew Mask Regulator Supply Hose — Removal

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Removal of the crew mask supply hose at one flight crew station, including depressurisation of the oxygen line, disconnection at the regulator manifold and examination of the hose pressure carrier.

sections.purpose: This task gives the procedure to remove the crew mask supply hose at one flight crew station for replacement or for inspection of the hose cover and pressure carrier.
sections.job_setup_note: Oxygen work needs a clean area. Make sure no oil, grease or solvent is present at the work position and that the technician's hands and gloves are free of hydrocarbons. Close the crew oxygen supply and depressurise the line before any connection is broken. Get the oxygen approved capping set. Do not use a lubricant of any kind on an oxygen fitting.
sections.procedure: 1. Put the warning notices in the flight compartment and tell the crew that the crew oxygen system is unserviceable. 2. WARNING: OXYGEN UNDER PRESSURE WITH OIL OR GREASE CAN CAUSE AN EXPLOSION. KEEP THE WORK AREA AND ALL TOOLS FREE OF HYDROCARBONS. 3. Close the crew oxygen supply valve. 4. Depressurise the line at the regulator test port and confirm zero pressure on the gauge. 5. Remove the console side panel at the affected station. 6. Disconnect the hose at the mask end and cap the fitting. 7. Disconnect the hose at the regulator manifold and cap both open connections immediately. 8. CAUTION: DO NOT LET THE HOSE END TOUCH THE FLOOR. CONTAMINATION AT THE FITTING CANNOT BE CLEANED IN SITU AND THE HOSE WILL BE REJECTED. 9. Release the hose from the stowage guide and remove it from the console. 10. Examine the hose cover along the stowed section and record any abrasion depth against the limits in the table. 11. Put the hose in a clean bag with its record card.
sections.close_out: Leave the capping plugs in position and the oxygen supply valve closed until the installation task is complete. Leave the warning notices in the flight compartment. Record the removal, the hose part number and the abrasion finding in the aircraft technical log.

safety_precautions: Keep the work area and all tools free of oil, grease and solvent.
Close the crew oxygen supply valve and confirm zero pressure before any connection is broken.
